blocks.content: Course: API Handling with Asynchronous Javascript
In the background, JavaScript keeps track of which function is currently running and what needs to run next using a structure called the call stack.
Imagine a stack of books where you place one book on top of another. Naturally, you can only pick up or remove the book on the top.
You can't pull one from the middle without first moving the books above it, or the whole stack might collapse.
This behavior is called Last In, First Out (LIFO).

items: A function is pushed onto the stack
When it finishes, it is popped off the stack

blocks.content: JavaScript always executes the function that's on top of the stack. Nothing else can run until that function finishes.
